verses.1: Elisha said to the woman who had kept her son alive, “Get up and go with your household. Live in the place where you will be living. For Jehovah has declared a famine in that land for seven years.”
verses.2: And the woman rose up and did as the man of God commanded her. She went away from her house, and she lived in the land of Canaan for seven years.
verses.3: And it was after seven years that the woman returned from the land of Palestine. She went out and cried out to the king, to his house, and to her field.
verses.4: And the king said to Geshai, a young man who was a servant of God: “Tell me all about the great things that Elisha did.”
verses.5: And he told the king about the woman who had lived after her son died. Then the woman cried out to the king, “Look at my house and my field!” The king said, “Take this woman and her son as prisoners.” This was Eliezer’s son.
verses.6: And the king asked for a woman. She was given to him, and the king gave her one censer, saying, “Return all that belongs to her, along with all the offerings from the field since she left the land from the day she departed until now.”
verses.7: And Elijah came, along with Ben-Hadad, king of Aram. He reported to them, “A man from God has arrived.”
verses.8: And the king said to Hizkiah, “Take some food in your hand and go to the Lord. Ask Him to heal you from this disease.”
verses.9: And Hizael went to call him. He took some food with him, along with all kinds of good things. He brought forty guldenes with him. Then he came and stood before him. He said, “You are the son of Haddad, king of Aram. I have sent for you because I want you to heal me from this illness.”
verses.10: And Elisha said to him, “Go and say to him, ‘You will live.’ And let the LORD see that he will indeed die.”
verses.11: And he faced forward, and he put on his armor. Then he stood as a man of God.
verses.12: And Hizkiah said, “What shall I do, my Lord?” He replied, “I know that you will do harm to the children of Israel. You will send fire upon them, and destruction upon their homes. They will be destroyed, and their possessions will be plundered.”
verses.13: And Hizael said, “What will your servant do? What can he do in order to accomplish such a great task?” And Elisha said, “Look, God has appointed you king over Aram.”
verses.14: And he went from Elisha’s place, and came before his master. He said to him, “What did Elisha say to you?” The master replied, “He said, ‘You will live.’”
verses.15: And in the evening, the king took a bath and bathed in the water. Then he washed his face and died. And Hazael became king in his place.
verses.16: And in the fifth year of Jeroboam son of Ahaz, king of Israel, and Yehoshaphat was king of Judah. Jeroboam son of Yehoshaphat was king of Judah.
verses.17: He ruled for thirty-two years. He was king in Jerusalem for two years.
verses.18: And he went along the path of the kings of Israel, just as Ahaz did. Ahaz married a daughter of Ahaziah, but he did evil in the eyes of Jehovah.
verses.19: And Jehovah did not want to destroy the Jews, so that David, His servant, could give him land for his children to live in, as He had promised him.
verses.20: In those days, Adam sinned under the rule of Judah. And a king ruled over them.
verses.21: And Yoram, a young man, and all the soldiers with him passed by. In the morning, he went out and attacked the people living around him, along with their leaders. The people fled into their camp.
verses.22: And Adam sinned under the authority of Judah, up to this day. Then, in this time, Cain also sinned.
verses.23: And all the words of Yoram, and everything he did, are recorded in the book of the days of the kings of Judah.
verses.24: And Yoram lay down with his fathers. He was buried with his fathers in the city of David. Ahaziah, his son, became king after him.
verses.25: In the twenty-third year of Jehoshaphat, son of Ahaziah, king of Israel, Ahaziah, son of Jehoahaz, king of Judah, reigned.
verses.26: At the age of forty-one, he became king. He ruled for one year in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Atalia, daughter of Amri, king of Israel.
verses.27: And he went along the path of Abi’ah. He did evil in the eyes of Jehovah, just as Abi’ah had done. For Abi’ah was a man who committed evil deeds.
verses.28: And Joram son of Ahahab went to war against Hazael, king of Aram, at Ramoth Gilead. And the people of Aram defeated Joram.
verses.29: And King Yoram went to Israel to recover from the wounds he suffered at Armim’s hands during his battle against King Hazael. He was captured by Jehu, son of Jehoiada. Yoram went down to see Yoram, son of Achab, in Israel. It seemed that he was sick.
